name: Acute Myeloid Leukemia and Myelodysplastic Syndromes Related to Topoisomerase Type 2 Inhibitor
aliases: Therapy-related AML/MDS due to Topoisomerase II Inhibitors
Topoisomerase II Inhibitor-associated Acute Myeloid Leukemia and Myelodysplastic Syndromes

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: WHO Classification of Tumors of Hematopoietic and Lymphoid Tissues (2016)

criteria.description: History of prior exposure to topoisomerase II inhibitors (e.g., etoposide, doxorubicin)
Presence of ≥20% myeloblasts in bone marrow or peripheral blood
Detection of characteristic balanced chromosomal translocations involving 11q23 (MLL gene) or other topoisomerase II inhibitor-associated abnormalities
Evidence of dysplastic changes in one or more myeloid cell lines consistent with myelodysplastic syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: History of topoisomerase II inhibitor exposure plus ≥20% myeloblasts in bone marrow or blood with characteristic cytogenetic abnormalities
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Latency period typically 1-3 years after exposure; diagnosis requires exclusion of de novo AML/MDS.

pathognomonic.notes: Presence of immature myeloid cells in peripheral blood is highly indicative
searchTerms: low blood counts with immature cells
reduced blood cells with blasts in blood

pathognomonic.symptomName: Bone marrow hypercellularity with dysplastic hematopoiesis
searchTerms: bone marrow crowded with abnormal cells

common.symptomName: Anemia-related pallor and dyspnea on exertion
searchTerms: pale skin and shortness of breath

common.notes: Neutropenia predisposes to bacterial and fungal infections
searchTerms: recurrent infections due to immune weakness
infections caused by low white blood cells

common.symptomName: Easy bruising and mucocutaneous bleeding from thrombocytopenia
common.notes: Platelet deficiency leads to bleeding diathesis
searchTerms: easy bruising and bleeding from low platelets

common.notes: May reflect leukemic infiltration or infection
searchTerms: temperature rise with no infection found

occasional.notes: Less common in AML compared to lymphoid leukemias

rare.symptomName: Central nervous system involvement with neurological deficits
searchTerms: nerve deficits due to CNS involvement

rare.notes: Due to high circulating blast counts
searchTerms: lung problems from blood cell buildup

rare.notes: Particularly in acute promyelocytic leukemia subtype

laboratory: Peripheral blood smear showing circulating myeloblasts
Bone marrow biopsy with hypercellularity and dysplasia
imaging: Chest X-ray may show infiltrates or leukostasis
CT scan for hepatosplenomegaly or lymphadenopathy
genetic: Balanced chromosomal translocations involving 11q23 (MLL gene rearrangements)
Other topoisomerase II inhibitor-associated cytogenetic abnormalities (e.g., t(8;21), inv(16))
other: History of prior chemotherapy with topoisomerase II inhibitors

distinguishingFeatures: No prior exposure to topoisomerase II inhibitors

redFlags: Rapid onset of pancytopenia with circulating blasts
History of recent chemotherapy with topoisomerase II inhibitors
references: Arber DA, et al. The 2016 revision to the World Health Organization classification of myeloid neoplasms and acute leukemia. Blood. 2016.
Smith SM, Le Beau MM, Huo D, et al. Clinical-cytogenetic associations in 306 patients with therapy-related myelodysplasia and acute myeloid leukemia: the University of Chicago series. Blood. 2003.
